FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Jute Mill Machinery/Accessories and Spare Parts Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This first part of the standard covers the specification for spool centres for spool winding machines. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requiremen t of this standard is complied with the final value. observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with ]S 2: 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value shall be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TEXTILE MACHINERY AND ACCBSSORIESCROSS WOUND SPOOL CENTRES FOR JUTE WINDING MACHINES - SPECIFICATION
PART 2 SPOOL CENTRES FOR PRECISION WINDING MACHINES
1 SCOPE Thi s standard prescribes the requirement s of cylind rica l and conical spool centres for use in d ifferent type s of jute prec ision winding ma ch ines. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are ne ce ssary ad junct s to this sta nd a rd : IS No. Title 196 : 1966 Atmospheric cond itions for testing (rel'ised) 707: 1976 Glossary of terms applicable to timber technology and utilization ( second revision ) Code of practice of seasoning 1141 : 1973 of t imber (first revision) 2500 Sampling in sp ection tables: ( Pa rt I) : 1973 Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by co u n t of defects (first revision) 3 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Material Th e sp oo l centre may be made of paper. synt hetic material or any of the species of timber listed in Annex A in accordance with the contract or order. 3.1.1 T imber used for the manufacture of spool cent res shall be seasoned (see IS 1141 : 1973 ) before use. 3.1.2 Wooden spool centres sha ll be free from visible defects such as checks, splits, gum veins, bark pockets, hole or any other defect which is likely to affect the life or usefulness (for the de scription of defects see IS 707 : 1976 ). The surface shall be sanded smooth. 3.1.3 Synthetic a s well as paper spoo l centres sha ll have un iformly distributed embossing on the surfac e. 4 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS Tables I and '2 when read with Fig. I and 2 respectively in accordance with the contract or order. 4.2 Concentricity The spool centres shall be concentric, the concentricity of spool centres shall, however, not exceed 1'5 mm in case of cylindrical spool centres and OoS mm in case of conical spool centres. 4.3 Position of the Groove in C~'lindrical Spool Centre The distance between the groove and the end shall be same at both the end s of cyl indrical spool centres (see Fig. I ).

5 METHOD OF TEST
5.1 The dimensions, ma ss and concentricity of the spool centres shall be checked by the use o f suitable calipers, gauges and balance.

5.2 In case of dispute or if agreed to between the buyer and the seller, the test sample shall be conditioned to moisture equilibrium and tested in the standard atmospheric conditions, that is ( 65 � 2 ) percent relative humidity and 27 == 2�C temperature ( see also IS 196 : ]966 ). 6 MARKING 6.1 Each spool centre shall be marked with the following informa tions: a) Indication of the source of manufacture; b) Date of manufacture; c) Batch number; and d) Dimensiens .ofthe spool. 6.1.1 The spool centres may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

7 PACKING
7.1 The spool centres shall be packed in accordance with the agreement between the buyer and the seller.

8 SAMPUNG AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer to ascertain the conformity of the spool centres for jute winding machines to the requirements of this specification, single sampling plan with Inspection Level 1 and Acceptance Quality Level (AQL) of 2�5 percent given in Tables I and 2 of IS 2500 ( Part I ) : 1973 shall be followed.

S...... Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau 0/ Indian Standards Act, ]986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produc~d to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of , InSpectIon, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated , by th.e producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for confornuty to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for t.he use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtamed from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
